message.content:
**Decision: Buy — order filled.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business that is growing modestly but with improving profitability and very strong cash generation: total net sales of $391.0B (up 2% from $383.3B), with Services up 13% to $96.2B and total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income rose to $123.2B from $114.3B, and operating cash flow was $118.3B. Net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 were slightly below FY2023 ($97.0B / $6.13) only because of a one-time, non-cash-like $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), which I treat as a non-recurring item rather than a deterioration in the franchise; the company also returned ~$110B to shareholders ($95.0B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends) and holds $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. Risks I noted are real but not disqualifying — Greater China net sales fell 8%, iPhone revenue was flat, and there is ongoing DMA/DOJ/Epic antitrust and regulatory exposure — so I sized the position modestly rather than aggressively. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.90 — a limit about 0.1% above the market, effectively at-the-market — which filled at $222.90 for a total of roughly $9,808. That is within the $10,000 per-order cap, brings today's total purchases to about $9,808 (well under the $20,000 daily cap), uses only existing cash (no money moved out of the account), and stays inside the AAPL/MSFT, buy-only mandate.
